stages.reference:
Create a close material reference for rough natural gravel from a weather-beaten dark-fantasy landscape.

The ground is an unsorted accumulation of fractured local stone: angular chips mixed with worn pieces, grit and packed dust. Individual stones should feel geologically related but not identical, with restrained differences in value, mineral tone and abrasion. Fine material settles between larger fragments so the surface feels compact enough to walk on rather than like a decorative bag of pebbles.

Favor muted gray, taupe and earthy mineral tones. Avoid uniformly round aquarium gravel, perfectly separated stones, high-contrast black-and-white noise, wet shine or oversized rocks.

Build a believable language of crushed, traveled-over ground whose age comes from abrasion, dust and compression. Do not arrange it as a repeating game tile.
